title: Condensation, GCH, and Diamond in L

items.title: Canonical Skolem hulls in constructible levels
items.statement: For a limit level L_alpha and A subseteq L_alpha, Hull^{L_alpha}(A) is the omega-stage closure of A under the <_L-least witness in L_alpha for every formula and finite parameter tuple. The fixed formula enumeration and canonical L-order make the operation specified without ambient Choice.
items.strategy: Define the successive closures from set-coded satisfaction and the canonical order. The next lemma supplies set existence, elementarity, and size, so the definition does not presume its own well-definedness.

references.title: Lietz, Set Theory, Lemma 7.11, pp. 57–58

items.title: Canonical L-hulls are elementary and small
items.statement: In ZF, Hull^{L_alpha}(A) is elementary in L_alpha. If A is infinite and well-orderable, the hull is well-orderable of cardinality at most |A|; if A is finite, it is countable.
items.strategy: Induct through the omega closure, coding new elements by a formula number and finite tuple from the prior stage; Hessenberg absorption gives the bound. Closure under every least-witness function proves the Tarski–Vaught criterion. No arbitrary family of choices is selected.

references.title: Kunen, Set Theory, Chapter VI §5, pp. 177–179

items.title: Condensation for constructible levels
items.statement: If alpha is a nonzero limit ordinal, X is elementary in L_alpha, and pi:X to M is the Mostowski collapse, then M=L_beta for beta=Ord intersect M. The collapse fixes every transitive part contained in X.
items.strategy: Collapse X, then use the fixed finite theory characterizing L-levels and absoluteness of the L-recursion to identify the collapsed hierarchy below beta. The internal V=L clause exhausts M. This uses only finite reflection, not a truth predicate for L.

references.title: Lietz, Set Theory, Lemma 7.11, pp. 57–58
Kunen, Set Theory, Chapter VI Theorems 3.8–3.9, pp. 171–172

items.title: Cardinality of infinite constructible levels
items.statement: ZF proves that for every infinite ordinal alpha, L_alpha is well-orderable and |L_alpha|=|alpha|.
items.strategy: Induct on alpha. At successors code definable subsets by formula numbers and finite parameter tuples; at limits tag each element by its least earlier stage. Use only arithmetic of well-orderable cardinals, so ambient AC is unnecessary.

references.title: Lietz, Set Theory, Proposition 7.14, p. 59; Kunen VI.1.14 and Exercise 1

items.title: Definable subsets of a constructible level are small
items.statement: For infinite alpha, Def(L_alpha) is well-orderable and has cardinality |alpha|.
items.strategy: Assign each definable subset its least formula code and least finite parameter tuple in the canonical order, injecting Def(L_alpha) into omega times L_alpha^{<omega}. Definable singletons give the reverse inequality.

references.title: Kunen, Set Theory, Chapter VI Lemmas 1.1–1.3, pp. 165–166

items.title: Constructible subsets appear before successor cardinals
items.statement: In ZF, if kappa is an infinite cardinal and x is constructible with x subseteq kappa, then x belongs to L_{kappa^+}. More generally every constructible subset of L_kappa appears in some L_beta with beta<kappa^+.
items.strategy: Take a sufficiently reflective L_theta containing x and kappa. For x subseteq kappa, form the canonical hull of kappa union {x}; for the general x subseteq L_kappa clause, form the hull of L_kappa union {x}. Condensation yields L_beta, and the collapse fixes the included transitive part pointwise and hence fixes x. The hull-size bound gives |beta|<=kappa, hence beta<kappa^+.

references.title: Lietz, Set Theory, Theorem 7.15, p. 59
Kunen, Set Theory, Chapter VI Theorem 4.6, p. 175

items.title: The generalized continuum hypothesis holds in L
items.statement: ZF proves that L satisfies GCH; equivalently, ZF proves V=L implies AC+GCH.
items.strategy: Work internally in L, where the published theorem supplies AC. Every subset of an infinite L-cardinal kappa lies in L_{kappa^+}, whose size is kappa^+; Cantor supplies the lower bound. AC is used only inside L to well-order power sets and interpret cardinal exponentiation.
items.axiom_base: ZF; AC is derived internally in L

references.title: Lietz, Set Theory, Theorem 7.15, p. 59; Kunen VI.4.6–4.8

items.title: V equals L implies diamond
items.statement: ZF proves V=L implies diamond on omega_1. For every A subseteq omega_1, the correct-guess set is stationary, not merely unbounded.
items.strategy: Choose the sequence by <_L-least local counterexamples. Given a target A and club C witnessing failure, take the canonical countable hull of their parameters in a suitable L_theta. Condensation, collapse-fixing, elementarity, and <_L-absoluteness identify the local pair at delta=X intersect omega_1 with the restrictions of A and C, while closure gives delta in C, a contradiction. Canonical witnesses avoid ambient AC.

references.title: Lietz, Set Theory, Definition 7.17 and Theorem 7.20, pp. 60–61
Kunen, Set Theory, Chapter VI Theorem 5.2, pp. 177–179

items.title: V equals L gives a Suslin tree
items.statement: ZF proves that V=L implies the existence of a normal splitting Suslin tree on omega_1.
items.strategy: Apply diamond and the published diamond-to-Suslin construction. That construction invokes AC for countable-union, maximal-antichain, and deterministic well-ordering steps; V=L supplies exactly that hypothesis.

references.title: Lietz, Set Theory, Theorem 7.20, pp. 60–61

items.title: Finite-fragment interpretation in L with GCH
items.statement: For each fixed finite fragment Delta of ZFC+GCH, some finite fragment Gamma of ZF proves the L-relativization of every member of Delta, with an effective translation of finite derivations.
items.strategy: Collect the finitely many ZF instances used by the axiom-by-axiom L proofs and by GCH, plus the fixed recursive definitions and syntactic relativization clauses. External finiteness yields one Gamma and a primitive-recursive proof translation, without a truth predicate or a full transitive model.

references.title: Kunen, Set Theory, Chapter VI §§2–4, pp. 169–176
UCLA 220C notes, Constructible Sets §8, pp. 293–295

items.title: Formal consistency of ZFC plus GCH relative to ZF
items.statement: For the fixed arithmetizations, a verified proof transformation establishes Con(ZF) implies Con(ZFC+GCH). It does not assume a transitive set model of ZF.
items.strategy: Translate an alleged finite ZFC+GCH contradiction proof through L. Its finite support is handled by the preceding lemma, producing a ZF contradiction proof. Apply the published verified proof-reduction theorem contrapositively.

references.title: Kunen, Set Theory, Chapter VI Corollary 4.9, p. 175
UCLA 220C notes, Constructible Sets §8, pp. 293–295

items.title: Positive relative consistency of CH and GCH
items.statement: Con(ZF) implies Con(ZFC+GCH) and Con(ZFC+CH); consequently Con(ZFC) implies both positive consistency statements.
items.strategy: Use the preceding theorem for GCH, then syntactically weaken to its omega instance CH. For the final formulation, any ZF contradiction would also be a ZFC contradiction, so Con(ZFC) implies Con(ZF).

references.title: Kunen, Set Theory, Chapter VI Corollary 4.9, p. 175

title: Condensation, GCH, and Diamond in L: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Condensation bounds a constructible real
items.statement: For x subseteq omega with x in L, the hull-and-collapse argument produces a countable beta<omega_1 with x in L_beta.
items.strategy: Choose L_theta containing x, close omega union {x}, collapse to L_beta, use omega subseteq the hull to fix every natural number, and then use extensionality to fix x. Countability of the hull makes beta countable.

references.title: Lietz, Set Theory, Theorem 7.15, p. 59

items.title: A diamond guess seals a maximal antichain
items.statement: At a countable limit stage delta of the diamond Suslin-tree construction, a correctly guessed maximal antichain in T_{<delta} is sealed by placing the new level above branches meeting that antichain.
items.strategy: Verify the partial tree is countable, use the published covering-branch lemma, and show every later node is above an antichain member. Identify the published construction's AC uses; V=L supplies them.
items.axiom_base: ZF under V=L; derived AC is used

references.title: Lietz, Set Theory, Theorem 7.20, pp. 60–61

items.title: False statement: ZF proves L equals V
items.statement: False statement: because ZF proves L is an inner model of ZFC+V=L, ZF therefore proves V=L.
items.strategy: Expose the quantifier-domain error: relativized axioms and L subseteq V do not give V subseteq L. A full metamathematical refutation of ZF proving V=L needs the later negative forcing consistency transfer; importing it here would be a forbidden forward dependency, so this item is escalated.

references.title: Kunen, Set Theory, warning after Chapter VI Corollary 3.4, pp. 170–171

title: The Forcing Theorem and Formal Consistency Transfer

items.title: Atomic forcing relation
items.statement: Define forced subset by density below p of conditions witnessing membership, forced equality by two subset clauses, and forced membership by density below p of coefficients whose subnames are forced equal. All clauses use q<=p for q stronger.
items.strategy: Give the simultaneous atomic clauses without semantic reference to M[G]. The next lemma establishes the rank recursion and agreement between internal and external definitions.

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, recursive definition and Claims 1–2, pp. 5–7

items.title: Atomic forcing is well-founded and definable
items.statement: The simultaneous atomic clauses have unique truth values by induction on name-rank pairs, and over a transitive ground model the internally defined relation agrees with the external recursion for its names.
items.strategy: Check every recursive call decreases the lexicographic pair (max rank, rank sum), apply setlike recursion, and compare internal/external definitions using rank absoluteness and bounded quantification. Cross-check the clauses with the published Boolean atomic semantics.

references.title: Karagila, Forcing, Definition 2.10 and Theorem 2.20, pp. 8–10

items.title: Forcing relation for all formulas
items.statement: Extend atomic forcing by formula complexity: conjunction is componentwise, negation means no stronger condition forces the subformula, and an existential is forced when conditions forcing an instance by some ground name are dense below p.
items.strategy: Use structural recursion on the finite formula code and verify name substitution is set-coded. The dense existential clause avoids any maximal-antichain mixing argument.

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, formula recursion, pp. 7–8

items.title: Monotonicity, density, and decision for forcing
items.statement: If p forces phi and q<=p, q forces phi. If forcing phi is dense below p, p forces phi. Below every p, conditions forcing phi or forcing not phi are dense.
items.strategy: Induct through the atomic recursion and formula complexity. For decision, below any condition either an extension forces phi or the condition forces not phi. Maintain the stronger-below convention.

references.title: Karagila, Forcing, Proposition 2.11 and Exercise 2.15, p. 8

items.title: Truth lemma
items.statement: For transitive M, P in M, M-generic G, formula phi, and names tau_i in M, M[G] satisfies phi(tau_i^G) iff some p in G forces phi(tau_i) in M.
items.strategy: Prove atomic membership and equality simultaneously by name-rank induction, using generic directedness and the dense clauses. Then induct on formulas: decision handles negation, and the definition of M[G] plus the dense witness clause handles existentials. No AC or maximal antichain is used.
items.axiom_base: ZF, conditional on a supplied generic

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, Forcing Theorem proof, pp. 5–8
Karagila, Forcing, Theorem 2.20, pp. 9–10

items.title: Forcing theorem
items.statement: For each formula, its forcing relation is uniformly definable over a transitive ground model and satisfies the truth lemma. If generics through every condition are externally available, p forces phi exactly when every such generic containing p makes phi true.
items.strategy: Combine recursion/definability with the truth lemma. For the semantic converse, an extension forcing not phi admits a generic under the explicit external enumeration hypothesis; do not silently assert generic existence for arbitrary grounds.
items.axiom_base: ZF; semantic converse conditional on available generics

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, Forcing Theorem, pp. 5–8
Karagila, Forcing, Theorem 2.20, pp. 9–10

items.title: Generic extensions satisfy ZF and preserve ground-model Choice
items.statement: If M is transitive ZF, P is in M, and G is M-generic, then M[G] is transitive ZF containing M and G. If M satisfies AC, M[G] satisfies AC. The ZF branch uses no ambient AC.
items.strategy: Use transitivity and canonical names for the basic axioms. Separation selects possible name-members by the definable forcing relation. Replacement chooses least-rank forced witnesses and bounds them in one name; Power Set similarly bounds subset names. For AC only, M well-orders a ground set of candidate names and the least representative order descends to their values.
items.axiom_base: ZF; the ZFC branch assumes M models AC

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, ZF and Choice verification, pp. 8–10
Karagila, Forcing, Theorem 2.21, pp. 10–11

items.title: Forcing preserves ordinals
items.statement: Under the generic-extension hypotheses, Ord intersect M[G]=Ord intersect M. Forcing may nevertheless change which ordinals are cardinals or cofinalities.
items.strategy: Check names put every ground ordinal in the extension. Conversely use transitivity and the valuation rank bound to bound any extension ordinal below a ground ordinal, then use downward closure of ordinals and transitivity of M.

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, ordinal preservation, pp. 10–11

items.title: Forcing equivalence and Boolean completion
items.statement: Every forcing preorder is forcing-equivalent to its separative quotient and the nonzero part of its regular-open complete Boolean algebra. Dense embeddings pull generics back and translate names so valuations and forced formulas agree. No BPI or AC is required.
items.strategy: Use the published choice-free regular-open construction. For a dense embedding, recursively translate names and prove valuation agreement, then apply the forcing theorem. Match Boolean values with regular opens and explicitly omit Boolean zero from the forcing order.

references.title: Karagila, Forcing, Theorems 2.31 and 2.34, pp. 11–13

items.title: Orientation for intermediate models and complete subalgebras
items.statement: For a complete subalgebra B subseteq C, a C-generic H pulls back to the B-generic H intersect B and M subseteq M[H intersect B] subseteq M[H]. The converse intermediate-model theorem needs extra proof and is not asserted.
items.strategy: Pull ground dense subsets of B through the complete inclusion and verify genericity. Record only the direction needed later so no consumer reverses the generic or model inclusions.

references.title: Karagila, Forcing, dense embeddings and projections, pp. 11–14

items.title: Semantic generic extensions of countable transitive models
items.statement: Given an externally countable transitive M satisfying ZFC, P in M, and p in P, an M-generic G containing p exists; M[G] is a countable transitive ZFC model with the same ordinals and satisfies exactly the formulas forced by members of G. The theorem is conditional on the CTM.
items.strategy: Use the supplied external enumeration of M to build G through p without ambient AC. Apply the forcing, extension-axiom, and ordinal theorems. Valuation maps the externally countable set of M-names onto M[G]. M's AC is used only for AC inside the extension.
items.axiom_base: ZF externally; conditional on a CTM of ZFC

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, generic extensions and forcing theorem, pp. 4–11
Karagila, Forcing, §§1.2 and 2.3–2.4, pp. 3–11

items.title: Forcing transfer for finite ZFC fragments
items.statement: For each fixed finite target fragment Delta whose axioms a specified P forces, a fixed finite source fragment Gamma of ZFC suffices to obtain a countable transitive Gamma-model, construct its generic extension, and verify Delta there.
items.strategy: Collect the finitely many Reflection, recursion, forcing, and extension-axiom instances used by Delta. ZFC supplies a CTM only of this fixed Gamma. Force over it and invoke the finite-fragment interface. Ambient AC is explicit because the published countable elementary-submodel construction uses it.

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, finite-fragment formalization, pp. 10–11

items.title: Formal consistency transfer by forcing
items.statement: For an effective target T, if a uniform formal forcing verification converts every finite T-proof support into the preceding finite-fragment construction, then Con(ZFC) implies Con(T). It does not infer a CTM of ZFC from Con(ZFC).
items.strategy: From a coded T contradiction proof compute its finite support and corresponding finite source fragment. The fragment construction yields a model of that support, or equivalently a primitive-recursive translation to a ZFC contradiction. Apply the published proof-reduction theorem, keeping CTMs confined to fixed reflected fragments.
items.axiom_base: formal arithmetic with effective proof predicates

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, finite-fragment relative-consistency argument, pp. 10–11

items.title: Relative consistency from a forced sentence
items.statement: If a uniform finite-fragment verification proves that a forcing P forces phi over ZFC, then Con(ZFC) implies Con(ZFC+phi). One supplied CTM and its semantic extension alone do not license this conclusion.
items.strategy: Take T=ZFC+phi in the formal transfer theorem. Each target contradiction proof has finite ZFC support plus phi, and the assumed uniform forcing verification handles exactly that finite support.

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, finite-fragment relative-consistency argument, pp. 10–11

title: The Forcing Theorem and Formal Consistency Transfer: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Atomic forcing of check names
items.statement: For ground x,y and every p, compute directly that p forces check x=check y iff x=y and p forces check x in check y iff x in y.
items.strategy: Induct simultaneously on membership ranks. Each check-name member occurs with every condition, so the dense atomic clauses reduce to the ground membership and equality statements.

references.title: Karagila, Forcing, Definitions 2.2 and 2.10, pp. 6, 8

items.title: Trivial forcing recovers the ground model
items.statement: For one-condition forcing, the unique generic evaluates every name to a ground set, M[G]=M, and forcing truth is ground-model truth.
items.strategy: Induct on name rank to show every valuation is a ground set and use check names for the converse inclusion, then apply the truth lemma.

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, names and forcing theorem, pp. 4–8

items.title: Forcing is not monotone toward weaker conditions
items.statement: In the forcing with weakest 1 and incompatible atoms p,q below it, p forces check p in dot G, while 1 does not. Thus monotonicity runs only to stronger conditions.
items.strategy: Evaluate the atomic membership clause. Below p the coefficient p is unavoidable, while q witnesses failure of density below 1. Compare with the correctly oriented monotonicity lemma.

references.title: Karagila, Forcing, stronger-below convention and Proposition 2.11, pp. 2, 8

items.title: Dense-equivalent forcing presentations
items.statement: For a finite preorder with duplicate mutually <=*-equivalent conditions, compute its separative quotient and regular-open completion and verify that all three presentations give the same generic extension.
items.strategy: List compatibility classes and downward regular opens, then write the generic pullback and recursive name translation explicitly. Keep embedding direction and removal of Boolean zero visible.

references.title: Karagila, Forcing, Proposition 1.5 and Theorems 2.31, 2.34, pp. 3, 11–13

items.title: False statement: the CTM presentation proves Con(ZFC)
items.statement: False statement: Con(ZFC) alone supplies a countable transitive model of all ZFC, so the semantic forcing presentation directly proves Con(ZFC) inside ZFC.
items.strategy: The semantic theorem is conditional on a CTM. Use the published CTM-versus-consistency boundary and second incompleteness to refute the asserted internal implication, then show that finite-fragment transfer repairs relative-consistency arguments without asserting a full CTM.

references.title: Neeman, Forcing, finite-fragment qualification, pp. 10–11
